claim: Egress is a discriminated union of six frozen Pydantic models, of which RaiseBoundaryError carries a refusal.
Every model, tool, memory and transport call runs inside an envelope whose egress half carries GOVERNANCE_AUTHORIZE and whose ingress half carries GOVERNANCE_VALIDATE.

ingress_governance_valid refuses a response kind outside four values, a next step outside five values, a correlation id of 0 or less, a correlation id not among the in-flight ids, a correlation id that is not the pending one, and a correlation id not greater than the last recorded one.
note: The function reads only kernel-local state: the in-flight set, the pending id and the last id. It reads no caller identity and no external record.

claim: A return that fails ingress_governance_valid closes the envelope with INGRESS_DENIED and returns RaiseBoundaryError(code='INGRESS_DENIED', recoverable=True).
Ingress governance is a first-match chain of plugins, and an empty chain falls back to one profile value.
The ingress profile acts only when response_kind is 'ERROR'; every other response kind returns ALLOW.
The governance answer is one of ten actions: ALLOW, BLOCK, TERMINATE, HITL, LOG, MODIFY, SKIP, RETRY, BLACKLIST and BACKTRACK.
note: BACKTRACK is produced only by boundary/gov/error_recovery.py, not by either profile table.

claim: The kernel maps seven ingress actions to a different result: HITL pauses, RETRY re-schedules the call up to max_gov_retries, BACKTRACK and BLOCK and TERMINATE raise boundary errors, and BLACKLIST and SKIP commit a rewritten return.
The egress chokepoint runs before the call and acts on HITL, BLOCK, TERMINATE, SKIP, BLACKLIST, RETRY and LOG, so a decision can hold, change or replace a call instead of only refusing it.
A BLOCK of a tool call writes the policy reason as a synthetic tool observation and schedules another model call, so the turn continues.
The code field of RaiseBoundaryError is a plain str with no enum and no pattern, so a boundary code is not held to any set.

claim: CONCORD's problem is several agents scoring one outcome on criteria that genuinely conflict, each correct from its own role.

All agents run the same protocol.

- **The initiator** is the agent that starts the run by sending `<concord-init>`. If it is listed in `<participants>`, it is also a participant; otherwise it does not negotiate. def _final_report(st):
    """The result, for the initiator to report to whoever asked for the run. Not a message to the agents: every
    agent reaches the same outcome from the same ratings."""
    tau = st["params"]["satisfaction_threshold"]
    winner = next(c for c in st["pool"] if c["id"] == st["x_star"])
    col = column(st, st["x_star"])
    lines = [f"RUN COMPLETE: outcome {st['outcome']}.",
             f"Winning candidate {winner['id']} (proposed by {winner['proposer']}): {winner['candidate']}",
             "Final scores: " + ", ".join(f"{a} {'no reply' if col[a] is None else '%.2f' % col[a]}"
                                         for a in st["agents"]) + f" (threshold {tau:g})"]
    short = {a: v for a, v in col.items() if v is not None and v < tau - TOL}
    if short:
        lines.append("Below the threshold: " + ", ".join(f"{a} by {tau - v:.2f}" for a, v in short.items()))
    unknown = absent(st, st["x_star"])
    if unknown:
        lines.append("Never rated (not certified): " + ", ".join(unknown))
    return "\n".join(lines)
